title: Continuity of family physician care and unplanned hospital admissions in older adults: a systematic review
subtitle: Evidence for a network decision on personal lists for patients aged 65 and over
statement: The network is considering personal lists so that patients aged 65 and over see their own family physician for most visits, which would lengthen waits for some patients. A systematic review of whether higher relational continuity is associated with fewer unplanned admissions in older adults, after accounting for illness severity, and whether deliberately raising continuity changes admissions, would inform the decision.
whoAffected: About 11,900 patients aged 65 and over in the network, their families, the 38 family physicians, and patients of all ages whose waits may lengthen.
whatHurts: Unplanned admissions are distressing and risky for older adults; losing a usual physician may mean missed deterioration, while longer waits may delay care for others.
currentPractice: Older patients are booked with whichever physician is free; continuity is not measured.
whyNow: A reorganisation proposal is before the network, and the committee has protected reviewer time this winter.
constraints: Three reviewers (two physicians and a nurse practitioner) with about 40 hours each from October 2026 to March 2027. No funding. Studies from primary care in high-income health systems, published in English.
patientCenteredGoal: Older patients have a physician who knows them, and changes to booking are made only if they help patients stay well at home without harming access for others.
summary: Problem framed as a systematic review to inform a network reorganisation.
